about: Pagila workload for tools/sample_db_bench.py. origin 'upstream-view': the CREATE VIEW bodies of upstream/pagila-schema.sql (name = upstream view name; rental_by_category is a materialized view created WITH NO DATA upstream), adapted to BigQuery SQL as 'adaptation' says; 'upstream-procedure': the SELECT statements of the upstream SQL and plpgsql functions with their parameters bound to the values in 'adaptation'; 'upstream-readme': the portable example queries of upstream's README.md; 'authored': written for this eval.

queries.name: actor_info
queries.adaptation: public. prefixes, ::text casts and the doubled parentheses of pg_dump dropped; jsonb_object_agg(c.name, titles) FILTER (WHERE c.name IS NOT NULL) becomes TO_JSON_STRING(ARRAY_AGG(STRUCT(c.name AS category, titles AS titles)) with NULL structs skipped), a JSON array of {category, titles} because BigQuery has no object aggregate; array_agg(f.title) gets ORDER BY f.title so the titles have a fixed order (upstream's order is unspecified)
features: correlated scalar subquery in an aggregate
queries.sql:
SELECT a.actor_id, a.first_name, a.last_name,
  TO_JSON_STRING(ARRAY_AGG(IF(c.name IS NOT NULL, STRUCT(c.name AS category, (SELECT ARRAY_AGG(f.title ORDER BY f.title) FROM film AS f JOIN film_category AS fc_1 ON f.film_id = fc_1.film_id JOIN film_actor AS fa_1 ON f.film_id = fa_1.film_id WHERE fc_1.category_id = c.category_id AND fa_1.actor_id = a.actor_id GROUP BY fa_1.actor_id) AS titles), NULL) IGNORE NULLS)) AS film_info
FROM actor AS a
LEFT JOIN film_actor AS fa ON a.actor_id = fa.actor_id
LEFT JOIN film_category AS fc ON fa.film_id = fc.film_id
LEFT JOIN category AS c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
GROUP BY a.actor_id, a.first_name, a.last_name

queries.name: customer_list
queries.adaptation: public. prefixes, ::text casts and the doubled parentheses of pg_dump dropped; the quoted alias "zip code" becomes `zip code`
queries.sql:
SELECT cu.customer_id AS id, cu.first_name || ' ' || cu.last_name AS name, a.address, a.postal_code AS `zip code`, a.phone, city.city, country.country,
  CASE WHEN cu.activebool THEN 'active' ELSE '' END AS notes, cu.store_id AS sid
FROM customer AS cu
JOIN address AS a ON cu.address_id = a.address_id
JOIN city ON a.city_id = city.city_id
JOIN country ON city.country_id = country.country_id

queries.name: film_list
queries.adaptation: public. prefixes, ::text casts and the doubled parentheses of pg_dump dropped; upstream's custom aggregate group_concat(text) (joins with ', ') becomes STRING_AGG(..., ', ' ORDER BY first_name, last_name, actor_id) so the string has a fixed order (upstream's order is unspecified)
queries.sql:
SELECT film.film_id AS fid, film.title, film.description, category.name AS category, film.rental_rate AS price, film.length, film.rating,
  STRING_AGG(actor.first_name || ' ' || actor.last_name, ', ' ORDER BY actor.first_name, actor.last_name, actor.actor_id) AS actors
FROM category
LEFT JOIN film_category ON category.category_id = film_category.category_id
LEFT JOIN film ON film_category.film_id = film.film_id
JOIN film_actor ON film.film_id = film_actor.film_id
JOIN actor ON film_actor.actor_id = actor.actor_id
GROUP BY film.film_id, film.title, film.description, category.name, film.rental_rate, film.length, film.rating

queries.name: nicer_but_slower_film_list
queries.adaptation: public. prefixes, ::text casts and the doubled parentheses of pg_dump dropped; group_concat becomes STRING_AGG with a fixed ORDER BY as in film_list; substring becomes SUBSTR
queries.sql:
SELECT film.film_id AS fid, film.title, film.description, category.name AS category, film.rental_rate AS price, film.length, film.rating,
  STRING_AGG(UPPER(SUBSTR(actor.first_name, 1, 1)) || LOWER(SUBSTR(actor.first_name, 2)) || UPPER(SUBSTR(actor.last_name, 1, 1)) || LOWER(SUBSTR(actor.last_name, 2)), ', ' ORDER BY actor.first_name, actor.last_name, actor.actor_id) AS actors
FROM category
LEFT JOIN film_category ON category.category_id = film_category.category_id
LEFT JOIN film ON film_category.film_id = film.film_id
JOIN film_actor ON film.film_id = film_actor.film_id
JOIN actor ON film_actor.actor_id = actor.actor_id
GROUP BY film.film_id, film.title, film.description, category.name, film.rental_rate, film.length, film.rating

queries.name: sales_by_film_category
queries.adaptation: public. prefixes, ::text casts and the doubled parentheses of pg_dump dropped
queries.sql:
SELECT c.name AS category, SUM(p.amount) AS total_sales
FROM payment AS p
JOIN rental AS r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
JOIN inventory AS i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
JOIN film AS f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
JOIN film_category AS fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id
JOIN category AS c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
GROUP BY c.name
ORDER BY SUM(p.amount) DESC

queries.name: rental_by_category
queries.adaptation: public. prefixes, ::text casts and the doubled parentheses of pg_dump dropped; upstream creates this materialized view WITH NO DATA, so it is empty there until refreshed: the query is run here on the loaded tables. Its body is the same as sales_by_film_category's, and both are kept
queries.sql:
SELECT c.name AS category, SUM(p.amount) AS total_sales
FROM payment AS p
JOIN rental AS r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
JOIN inventory AS i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
JOIN film AS f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
JOIN film_category AS fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id
JOIN category AS c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
GROUP BY c.name
ORDER BY SUM(p.amount) DESC

queries.name: sales_by_store
queries.adaptation: public. prefixes, ::text casts and the doubled parentheses of pg_dump dropped
queries.sql:
SELECT c.city || ',' || cy.country AS store, m.first_name || ' ' || m.last_name AS manager, SUM(p.amount) AS total_sales
FROM payment AS p
JOIN rental AS r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
JOIN inventory AS i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
JOIN store AS s ON i.store_id = s.store_id
JOIN address AS a ON s.address_id = a.address_id
JOIN city AS c ON a.city_id = c.city_id
JOIN country AS cy ON c.country_id = cy.country_id
JOIN staff AS m ON s.manager_staff_id = m.staff_id
GROUP BY cy.country, c.city, s.store_id, m.first_name, m.last_name
ORDER BY cy.country, c.city

queries.adaptation: body of film_in_stock with $1 = 1 (film) and $2 = 1 (store); inventory_in_stock(inventory_id) (a plpgsql function) is inlined as 'no rental of the item has a NULL return_date': its two branches (no rentals, or no rental with a NULL return_date) both reduce to that
queries.sql:

FROM inventory
WHERE film_id = 1
AND store_id = 1
AND (SELECT COUNT(rental.rental_id) FROM rental WHERE rental.inventory_id = inventory.inventory_id AND rental.return_date IS NULL) = 0

queries.adaptation: body of film_not_in_stock with $1 = 1 and $2 = 1; inventory_in_stock(inventory_id) (a plpgsql function) is inlined as 'no rental of the item has a NULL return_date': its two branches (no rentals, or no rental with a NULL return_date) both reduce to that
queries.sql:

FROM inventory
WHERE film_id = 1
AND store_id = 1

queries.adaptation: first SELECT of get_customer_balance with p_customer_id = 380 and p_effective_date = 2026-06-30 (a DATETIME literal; the timestamptz parameter is UTC); the second SELECT (late fees as interval arithmetic) is not adapted

queries.adaptation: the INSERT's SELECT of rewards_report (built as dynamic SQL there) with last_month_start = 2026-05-01, last_month_end = 2026-05-31, min_dollar_amount_purchased = 15.00 and min_monthly_purchases = 2 bound
queries.sql:
SELECT p.customer_id
FROM payment AS p
WHERE DATE(p.payment_date) BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-01' AND DATE '2026-05-31'
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING SUM(p.amount) > 15.00
AND COUNT(customer_id) > 2

queries.adaptation: the two statements of rewards_report as one query: the temporary table tmpCustomer is replaced by the INSERT's SELECT as a derived table, then 'SELECT c.* FROM tmpCustomer AS t INNER JOIN customer AS c ON t.customer_id = c.customer_id'; parameters bound as in pg-func-rewards-report-candidates
queries.sql:
SELECT c.*
FROM (
  SELECT p.customer_id
  FROM payment AS p
  WHERE DATE(p.payment_date) BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-01' AND DATE '2026-05-31'
  GROUP BY customer_id
  HAVING SUM(p.amount) > 15.00
  AND COUNT(customer_id) > 2
) AS t
INNER JOIN customer AS c ON t.customer_id = c.customer_id

queries.adaptation: README 'Find late rentals': CURRENT_DATE is cast to DATETIME to compare with the DATETIME column; LIMIT 5 dropped because many rentals share a title, so which five rows come back is not determined
queries.sql:
SELECT CONCAT(customer.last_name, ', ', customer.first_name) AS customer, address.phone, film.title
FROM rental
INNER JOIN customer ON rental.customer_id = customer.customer_id
INNER JOIN address ON customer.address_id = address.address_id
INNER JOIN inventory ON rental.inventory_id = inventory.inventory_id
INNER JOIN film ON inventory.film_id = film.film_id
WHERE rental.return_date IS NULL
AND rental_date < CAST(CURRENT_DATE AS DATETIME)
ORDER BY title

SELECT f.film_id, f.title, l.name AS language
FROM film AS f

WHERE f.rating = 'PG'

SELECT f.film_id, f.title, o.name AS original_language
FROM film AS f
LEFT JOIN language AS o ON f.original_language_id = o.language_id
WHERE f.length > 150

SELECT f.film_id, f.title
FROM film AS f
JOIN language AS o ON f.original_language_id = o.language_id

SELECT r.rental_id, c.last_name, f.title
FROM rental AS r
JOIN customer AS c ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN inventory AS i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
JOIN film AS f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
WHERE r.return_date IS NULL

SELECT c.customer_id, c.last_name, COUNT(*) AS rentals
FROM customer AS c
JOIN rental AS r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.last_name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 90

SELECT DISTINCT c.customer_id, c.first_name

JOIN rental AS r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id

SELECT DISTINCT fa.actor_id, fa.film_id
FROM film_actor AS fa
JOIN actor AS a ON fa.actor_id = a.actor_id

SELECT f.film_id, f.title
FROM film AS f
WHERE f.film_id IN (SELECT i.film_id FROM inventory AS i WHERE i.store_id = 2)

SELECT c.customer_id, c.last_name
FROM customer AS c
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payment AS p WHERE p.customer_id = c.customer_id AND p.amount > 10)

SELECT f.film_id, f.title
FROM film AS f
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM inventory AS i JOIN rental AS r ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id WHERE i.film_id = f.film_id
)

SELECT f.film_id
FROM film AS f
WHERE f.language_id NOT IN (SELECT g.original_language_id FROM film AS g)

SELECT f.film_id, f.title
FROM film AS f
WHERE f.film_id NOT IN (SELECT i.film_id FROM inventory AS i)

SELECT f.film_id, f.title, f.length
FROM film AS f
WHERE f.length > (SELECT AVG(g.length) FROM film AS g)

SELECT f.film_id, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM inventory AS i WHERE i.film_id = f.film_id) AS copies
FROM film AS f

SELECT film_id, title FROM film WHERE rating = 'G'
UNION ALL
SELECT film_id, title FROM film WHERE rating = 'NC-17'

SELECT city AS place FROM city
UNION DISTINCT
SELECT district AS place FROM address

SELECT customer_id FROM rental
INTERSECT DISTINCT
SELECT customer_id FROM payment

SELECT film_id FROM film
EXCEPT DISTINCT
SELECT film_id FROM inventory

SELECT film_id, rating, length, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY rating ORDER BY length DESC) AS length_rank
FROM film

SELECT customer_id, payment_id, amount,
  SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY payment_date, payment_id) AS running_total
FROM payment
WHERE customer_id <= 20

SELECT rental_id, rental_date,
  LAG(rental_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY rental_date, rental_id) AS previous_rental
FROM rental
WHERE customer_id = 1

WITH unused AS (SELECT * FROM staff),
long_films AS (SELECT film_id, title, length FROM film WHERE length > 180),
copies AS (SELECT film_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM inventory GROUP BY film_id)
SELECT l.title, c.n
FROM long_films AS l
JOIN copies AS c ON l.film_id = c.film_id

SELECT t.film_id, t.title
FROM (SELECT film_id, title, rating FROM film WHERE 1 = 1 AND TRUE) AS t
WHERE ((t.rating = 'R'))

SELECT c.customer_id,
  CASE WHEN c.activebool THEN 'active' WHEN c.active = 0 THEN 'closed' ELSE 'other' END AS state
FROM customer AS c

features: group by a key and its dependents
queries.sql:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(*) AS payments, SUM(p.amount) AS spent
FROM customer AS c
JOIN payment AS p ON p.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name

SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS films
FROM film AS f
GROUP BY f.rating
HAVING f.rating <> 'G'

SELECT customer_id, total
FROM (SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total FROM payment GROUP BY customer_id) AS t
WHERE customer_id < 10

SELECT DATETIME_TRUNC(payment_date, MONTH) AS month, SUM(amount) AS total
FROM payment

SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM create_date) AS signup_year, COUNT(*) AS customers
